stories.title: Labour’s split over Rosebank oilfield exposed by letter from nearly 100 MPs
stories.summary: Exclusive: Frontbenchers join scores of party colleagues urging Burnham not to let ministers approve project Opinion: Why Labour MPs are opposing Rosebank Podcast: are resignations next? Labour’s internal divisions over the giant Rosebank oilfield have spilled into the open, with nearly 100 Labour MPs – including a handful of frontbenchers – writing to the prime minister to express their opposition to the project. Ninety-two backbenchers and at least four frontbenchers have signed a letter to Andy Burnham urging him not to let his ministers approve the scheme for the biggest undeveloped field in UK waters. stories.title: At critical juncture, Friedrich Merz finds Germans’ support for Ukraine wavering
stories.summary: German chancellor is on difficult terrain, at home and abroad, as he fights to maintain European backing for Kyiv The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, is navigating choppy waters both at home and abroad over his insistence that Europe must keep up support – both military and financial – for Ukraine. At a Brussels summit on Thursday, Merz reiterated his view that all EU member states – pointedly, “not 23 or 24” – should support a €45bn (£38bn) loan for Ukraine for 2027. He has threatened to veto the bloc’s budget unless all countries sign up to the loan, a stance that saw him accused of “classic blackmail” by Robert Fico, the populist prime minister of Slovakia. Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria have also voiced their misgivings, to varying degrees, over Berlin’s dogged position. Continue reading...

stories.summary: Big lenders will aim to ‘protect their earnings’ amid temporary increase in corporation tax surcharge, says Andrew Bailey Business live – latest updates The governor of the Bank of England has warned that banks could look to pass on the £1.5bn cost of Labour’s increase to tax on their profits, a move that would put further pressure on household finances. John Healey, the chancellor, used his first budget last month to temporarily increase the bank corporation tax surcharge from 3% to 6% for a 15 month period from January, with the proceeds to be used to fund “breathing space” measures for households. stories.title: Heavy rain, wind and flooding hit much of US on Thanksgiving
stories.summary: Homes left without power and holiday travel disrupted as storms pound east coast and other parts of the US Storms have flooded communities in the US east coast, knocking out power to nearly a million customers and prompting the first-ever postponement of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade in New York City. High winds and flooding hammered both coasts, disrupting holiday travel. More than 900,000 homes and businesses were without electricity on Thursday evening, with the majority in east coast states, according to the outage tracking website PowerOutage.us. More than 2,200 flights to or from US destinations were delayed and more than 400 were cancelled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware. Continue reading...

stories.title: Natural England objected to a datacentre. Weeks later ministers threatened to abolish the agency
stories.summary: Body urged Bristol city council to reject plan because of risk to nearby protected wildlife and habitats Natural England objected to the building of a large AI datacentre near Bristol weeks before the government threatened to abolish the independent environmental adviser. The nature adviser made a significant intervention to urge Bristol city council not to grant planning permission for a 40MW datacentre at Avonmouth, because of the threat to protected wildlife and habitats at one of the UK’s most important sites for migratory birds, which is within 600 metres of the site.
